prompt.zh-TW: 阿哲把綠茵運動用品的「資本公積÷股本」算出來，發現比率很高，於是說：「市場給它的估值很高，可以買。」哪一個回應最恰當？
prompt.en: Che works out Greenfield Sports’ capital surplus divided by share capital, finds the ratio is high, and says: ‘The market values it highly, so it is a buy.’ Which response is the most appropriate?

text.zh-TW: 這個比率反映的是歷史發行溢價的累積，不是現在的市值
text.en: This ratio reflects issue premiums accumulated in the past, not today’s market value

feedback.zh-TW: 答對了。資本公積是過去某幾次發行股票時留下的紀錄，股價早已和它脫鉤；課程把它當成一種觀察方式，網站標為非標準比率。要看當下的市場估值，通常用股價算的本益比或股價淨值比，而這些比率也只是觀察的起點。
feedback.en: That is right. Capital surplus is a record left by past share issues, and the share price has long since decoupled from it; the course treats it as an observation, and the site marks it as a non-standard ratio. Today’s market valuation is usually read from the price-based P/E or price-to-book ratio, and even those are only a starting point.

text.zh-TW: 這是年報揭露的標準估值指標，比率高就是估值高
text.en: This is a standard valuation measure disclosed in annual reports; a high ratio means a high valuation

feedback.zh-TW: 你把它當成正式指標，這是常見誤會。年報的財務分析沒有這個比率；它是課程自訂的觀察方式。
feedback.en: Treating it as an official measure is a common misunderstanding. Annual report financial analysis does not include this ratio; it is an observation defined by the course.

text.zh-TW: 比率高代表公司最近幾年很賺錢，盈餘都累積在資本公積
text.en: A high ratio means profits from recent good years have built up in capital surplus

feedback.zh-TW: 你想把它和獲利連起來。但資本公積與盈餘無關，它來自股東投入；公司可能很久沒賺錢，比率仍然很高。
feedback.en: You are trying to link it to profit. But capital surplus has nothing to do with earnings; it comes from shareholder contributions, and the ratio can stay high even if the company has not made a profit for years.

explanation.zh-TW: {{option:o_k4m5}}說明了這個比率能看到什麼、看不到什麼。{{option:o_n6p7}}把課程的觀察方式當成標準指標；{{option:o_q8r9}}把投入資本和獲利混為一談。本章是會計觀念練習，不是投資建議。
explanation.en: {{option:o_k4m5}} explains what the ratio can and cannot show. {{option:o_n6p7}} mistakes a course observation for a standard measure; {{option:o_q8r9}} confuses contributed capital with profit. This chapter is an accounting concept exercise, not investment advice.
